question: Does a learned attention pooling inside a step combine token evidence better than the frozen top5 readout, with the teacher held fixed?

deviation_from_plan_section_11.reason: Omri excluded GPU self-supervision on 2026-09-23, so S4 is not run and its encoder does not exist.
deviation_from_plan_section_11.removed: the 11 masked-linear residual columns and the 32-dim SSL embedding, and with them the H_SSL and H_SSL_MEAN arms
deviation_from_plan_section_11.kept: the plan's own H_RAW arm (attention pooling over the raw token channels), the P_SOFT target, the role contract of plan 4.4, the optimizer settings of section 11, the B-fold global scale, and both primary endpoints
deviation_from_plan_section_11.not_answered: whether a learned SSL representation adds information; only the narrow pooling question is answered

representation.tokens: TOKEN_MATRICES.npz, 6,968,779 tokens x 11 float32 channels, token_offsets, step_spans (answer-relative); 6,963,312 tokens lie inside a step and are the only ones used
representation.normalization: per answer, per channel standardization over the answer's tokens (mean 0, SD 1; SD <= 1e-8 -> channel is all zeros)
representation.normalization_rationale: S2 finding: the frozen median/IQR normalization leaves top50_js, chosen_surprisal and true_tail50 with variance 1e6-3e9, so any channel-mixing pooling is otherwise dominated by three channels

base: plan 5.2 teacher (as S1/S2/S3): PB q_loc = mean_c softmax_s(Z); PRMB q_step = mean_c sigmoid(Z); Z = per-answer per-channel standardization of the frozen top5 step profile

arms.BASE: the teacher itself; fit-free, frozen readout top5 with equal channel weights
arms.H_TOP5: linear head u_s = w^T Z_s + b on the frozen top5 step profile, L-BFGS as plan 7.2 (this is the S1 P_SOFT student, recomputed here as the fixed-readout rung of the ladder)
arms.H_MEAN: same token features, uniform pooling attention_t = 1/n_tokens_s, AdamW as section 11
arms.H_RANDATT: attention of the same form with W, a, v frozen at random initialization; only the token-risk head is learned
arms.H_RAW: learned attention: k_t = tanh(W f_t + a) in R^32, attention_t = softmax_within_step(v^T k_t), token_risk_t = w^T f_t + b, u_s = sum_t attention_t * token_risk_t

target: P_SOFT only (PB q_loc, PRMB q_step); no gate, no confidence filtering, no teacher reselection after S1
loss: plan 7.2: PB weighted cross-entropy of q against log_softmax(u) over the answer's steps; PRMB weighted mean over steps of BCEWithLogits(u, q); answers drawn with the plan 5.3 weights

optimizer.neural_arms: AdamW, lr 1e-3, weight_decay 1e-4, 2000 updates, batch 16 answers sampled with replacement by the 5.3 weights, seeds 0/1/2, the LAST head is the result
optimizer.H_TOP5: L-BFGS from zero, ridge 0.01, maxiter 1000, gtol 1e-6, PB bias fixed at 0

scale: per head/seed, weighted mean and SD of u on B (answer mass divided by step count); final score = mean over the three seeds of (u - mu_B)/max(sd_B,1e-8); one global scale per fold/seed, no per-answer re-centering

splits.A: (k+3) mod 5 and (k+4) mod 5 - UNUSED in S5-CPU, because there is no encoder or transform to fit

secondary: each arm vs the fixed comparators
PB F1 with the frozen CT7 gate
PRMScore (C-calibrated; raw and per-answer z, per the S0-C rule)
diagnostics: attention entropy vs uniform, per task and depth stratum
attention mass on the first/last token of a step
correlation of attention with each raw channel
failure_policy: a non-finite u, a non-converged L-BFGS fit or a step with no tokens is a visible failure per (task, fold, seed); the affected H answers keep BASE and are reported as a separate baseline-preserving fallback row, never as native predictions
budget: <= 4 CPU-hours + evaluation; stop INCOMPLETE rather than truncate the training budget
interpretation: Attention is not a causal explanation. A gain must beat BOTH uniform pooling (H_MEAN, same optimizer and budget) and arbitrary attention of the same form (H_RANDATT); beating only BASE would confound learned pooling with learned channel weights.
